chunks: Similarly, the Muslim man who is free from dishonesty

expects one of the two good things from Allah: either a call [to death] from Allah, and whatever is with Allah is better for him, or the livelihood of Allah, in which case he is a man of family and wealth, and with him are his faith and lineage.
Certainly, wealth and children are the plantation of this world, and virtuous deeds are the plantation of the next world, and Allah may gather both for some people.

key_terms.الدَّاعِيَ: The caller (referring to death or the angel of death)
key_terms.حَرْثُ: Plantation or crop (metaphor for what is cultivated/produced)

ai.seo_question: What are the two good outcomes a Muslim free from dishonesty can expect from Allah?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) characterizes the believer free from treachery as one who awaits one of two 'goods': either death, which brings them closer to Allah's reward, or continued life with sustenance, preserving their faith and lineage. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and *tawakkul* (trust in God), framing worldly provisions not as ends in themselves but as means to maintain religious integrity. The hadith concludes by distinguishing between the 'crop' of this world (wealth and children) and the 'crop' of the Hereafter (righteous deeds), noting that Allah may grant both to the chosen.
